満.meaning: Rain falls in <part>water drops</part> on the pond until it rises over the <part>grass</part> at the edges, spilling out on <part>both</part> sides. Not one more drop will fit. The pond is <kanji>full</kanji>.
満.on: A thirsty <sound>mon</sound>key tries to drink it dry and gives up, its belly sloshing.
満.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat stands on tiptoe as the water fills up to its chin.

巾.meaning: A <part>pole</part> hangs down through a little <part>frame</part> on the bathroom wall, and something soft and fluffy drapes over it. Step out of the bath, reach over, rub your hair dry. It's a <kanji>towel</kanji>.
巾.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher dives into your bath and dries off on your towel.
巾.kun: You hang the towel over the kingfisher's cage under a big <sound>oa</sound>k tree: a cover.

席.meaning: In the corner of a <part>shed</part> there's an old crate with a <part>tray</part> on top and a folded <part>towel</part> for a cushion. Nobody else may sit there: it's Grandpa's, and he guards his <kanji>seat</kanji>.
席.on: He chalks a pie-chart <sound>sec</sound>tor on the floor around it, and nobody dares step inside.
席.kun: A <sound>moo</sound>se, a knight with a <sound>shi</sound>eld and a <sound>ro</sound>dent squeeze onto the mat beside him: a straw mat.

座.meaning: Under a <part>shed</part> roof, two friends spread out a <part>picnic</part> on the ground and plop down knees up. No chairs needed, no table either. They <kanji>squat</kanji> by the sandwiches all afternoon.
座.on: They squat there like traders at a ba<sound>za</sound>ar, selling off spare sandwiches.
座.kun: They sit down to <sound>su</sound>shi, and a baby cries '<sound>Wa</sound>h!' until she gets some.

帰.meaning: After years at sea, a sailor walks in the door with a <part>dagger</part> on his belt. His mum doesn't hug him first: she grabs her <part>feather duster</part> and dusts him from hat to boots. Then the hug. What a <kanji>homecoming</kanji>.
帰.on: He has lost his front door <sound>key</sound>, so he knocks with the handle of his dagger.
帰.kun: Mum cooks him <sound>ca</sound>rp and a fried <sound>e</sound>gg, the dish he always loved as a boy.

市.meaning: A <part>lid</part> of cloth stretched on poles makes an awning, and a <part>towel</part> hangs below with prices pinned on it. Under it someone sells apples, someone sells socks, someone yells 'Two for one!'. Welcome to the <kanji>market</kanji>.
市.on: A knight haggles for a dented <sound>shi</sound>eld at half price.
市.kun: An <sound>ee</sound>l sells fish at one stall, and a <sound>chee</sound>tah sells running shoes at the next.

姉.meaning: A <part>woman</part> marches you round the <part>market</part>, holding your hand tight and bossing you: 'Don't touch! Stay close!' She was born three years before you and never lets you forget it. She's your <kanji>elder sister</kanji>.
姉.on: She even bosses the knight at the stall: 'Polish that <sound>shi</sound>eld!'
姉.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, stop!' she yells, and catches you in a butterfly <sound>ne</sound>t before you can run off.

婦.meaning: On a packed train, a <part>woman</part> in white gloves pulls a <part>feather duster</part> from her handbag, dusts her seat before she sits, then dusts the seat beside her for a tired stranger. Not a crumb, not a rude word, a smile for everyone. A true <kanji>lady</kanji>.
婦.on: She even dusts the rolled-up <sound>fu</sound>ton a backpacker has wedged into the luggage rack.
婦.kun: Her stop is a wedding: she gets off with a <sound>yo</sound>gurt cake and a long <sound>me</sound>nu for the bride.
